svg.text: A leaky firewall: ufw and Docker
Concept 4 · on the VPS, packets for a container counter are diverted by Docker BEFORE the ufw rules are read
The way of a packet from the internet
VPS (Ubuntu): one network card, two ways
for a program on the machine
a program on the VPS, not a container: CHECKED by ufw
ufw is never asked about a diverted packet
Docker's documentation: container counters bypass the machine's firewall rules, ufw too. What decides who may knock is the address in ports:.
:1883 matches no line (its counter is only 127.0.0.1): not diverted, and nobody answers on the public IP.
anyone on the internet can knock on this counter
IPv4 only: an A record is enough in DNS, no AAAA
from the internet: unreachable (simulated lab: plain 1883
unreachable from outside, reachable from the VPS)
from the laptop: the tunnel ssh -L 5432:127.0.0.1:5432
The project's counters on the VPS (compose.cloud.yml + .env VPS column)
MQTT TLS: the Pi bridge, devices outside
plain: the backend through the hallway mosquitto:1883
ed25519 SSH key, password login off
ufw on the VPS: the order matters
22/tcp first: without it, ufw enable can lock out your own SSH.
ufw guards programs on the machine (sshd). The 80, 443, 8883 lines
are a note of intent: Docker still opens container counters itself.
ufw deny 1883 or ufw deny 5432 does NOT close a Docker counter.
Test from OUTSIDE (a phone, mobile data): MQTTX to mqtt.yourname.my.id:1883 fails.
Honestly: ufw and a real VPS weren't tested by the author; the order
comes from the Ubuntu and Docker docs, the 127.0.0.1 counters from the simulated lab.
